note: Regulatory entries are plain-English summaries written for this demo from the linked sources (checked 2026-10-28); re-check them before relying on them. Entries labelled mock policy are invented for the demo and are not any real bank's terms, rates or fees.

documents.title: Home loans: how they work
documents.keywords: home loan mortgage owner occupied investment property buy house
documents.text: A home loan is secured against the property. Owner-occupier loans are for a home you live in; investment loans are for property you rent out and usually carry a higher rate. Most loans run for up to 30 years with principal-and-interest repayments. Interest-only periods are available on some investment loans for up to 5 years, after which repayments rise to cover principal.

documents.title: Fixed and variable interest rates
documents.keywords: fixed variable rate interest split loan break cost offset redraw difference
documents.text: A variable rate can rise or fall over the life of the loan; it allows unlimited extra repayments, redraw and an offset account. A fixed rate stays the same for the fixed term, usually 1 to 5 years, so repayments are predictable; extra repayments are limited to 10,000 dollars a year and paying the loan out early, or switching, can trigger break costs. A split loan puts part of the balance on each. At the end of a fixed term the loan reverts to the variable rate unless the customer re-fixes.

documents.title: Current rates
documents.keywords: current interest rate home loan personal loan car loan percent comparison rate today
documents.text: Current rates: owner-occupied variable home loan 6.09 percent per annum; 2-year fixed home loan 5.79 percent per annum; unsecured personal loan from 7.99 percent per annum; secured car loan from 6.99 percent per annum. A customer's actual rate depends on assessment, loan-to-value ratio and product. Rates can change.

documents.title: Loan repayment options
documents.keywords: repayment weekly fortnightly monthly extra repayment redraw offset pay off early change repayment date
documents.text: Repayments can be weekly, fortnightly or monthly. Fortnightly repayments of half the monthly amount add up to roughly one extra monthly repayment a year. On variable loans, extra repayments are unlimited and can be redrawn later. An offset account reduces the balance interest is charged on. Customers can ask to change the repayment date or frequency; a change must not leave a repayment missed.

documents.title: Personal and car loans
documents.keywords: personal loan car loan secured unsecured borrow term establishment fee early repayment
documents.text: Personal loans range from 5,000 to 50,000 dollars over 1 to 7 years. A secured car loan uses the vehicle as security and usually has a lower rate than an unsecured loan. Fixed-rate personal loans have set repayments. The establishment fee is 250 dollars and there is no early repayment fee on variable personal loans.

documents.title: Loan fees and charges
documents.keywords: fee fees charge cost application establishment late payment monthly service break cost discharge
documents.text: Fee schedule: home loan application fee 0 dollars; home loan monthly service fee 8 dollars on basic variable loans and 0 dollars on package loans; discharge fee 350 dollars when a home loan is paid out; personal loan establishment fee 250 dollars; late payment fee 20 dollars. Fixed-rate break costs are calculated when the loan is broken and can't be estimated in advance.

documents.title: Applying for a loan
documents.keywords: apply application process steps how long approval conditional pre approval settlement specialist
documents.text: Applications start online, in a branch or with a lending specialist. The bank gives a credit guide, asks about the customer's requirements, objectives and finances, verifies them with documents, and runs a credit check with the customer's consent. A conditional pre-approval usually takes 2 to 5 business days once documents are in. Unconditional approval follows a property valuation. Only a credit assessor can approve a loan; a phone or chat assistant cannot approve credit or promise a borrowing amount.

documents.title: Eligibility and documents
documents.keywords: documents need eligibility payslips tax return statements identification deposit self employed requirements
documents.text: Applicants must be 18 or over and an Australian citizen or permanent resident for standard loans. Documents: photo identification; the two most recent payslips, or two years of tax returns and notices of assessment if self-employed; three months of savings or transaction statements; statements for other debts such as credit cards and car loans; evidence of the deposit; and for a purchase, the contract of sale.

documents.title: Responsible lending obligations
documents.source: National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009; ASIC RG 209
documents.keywords: responsible lending nccp assess unsuitable inquiries verify borrow how much approve credit assessment law
documents.text: Under the National Consumer Credit Protection Act, a lender must make reasonable inquiries about a customer's requirements and objectives and their financial situation, take reasonable steps to verify that situation, and assess whether the loan is not unsuitable. A loan is unsuitable if the customer couldn't meet the repayments, or could only do so with substantial hardship, or if it doesn't meet their requirements. The customer can ask for a copy of the assessment. ASIC Regulatory Guide 209 explains these obligations.

documents.title: Serviceability buffer
documents.keywords: buffer serviceability apra assess repayments higher rate borrowing capacity how much can i borrow
documents.text: APRA expects banks to check that a home loan borrower could still afford repayments if the interest rate were 3 percentage points higher than the loan's rate. That is why the amount a bank will lend can be lower than a simple repayment calculation suggests.

documents.title: Who regulates Australian banks
documents.source: ASIC, APRA, AFCA, OAIC, ABA Banking Code
documents.keywords: regulator regulation asic apra afca oaic banking code privacy law rules
documents.text: ASIC regulates conduct, including consumer credit and complaint handling. APRA regulates prudential soundness. AFCA, the Australian Financial Complaints Authority, resolves complaints a bank hasn't resolved, free of charge. The OAIC oversees privacy under the Privacy Act. Banks that subscribe to the Australian Banking Association's Banking Code of Practice also commit to its customer standards.

documents.title: Financial hardship: customer rights
documents.keywords: hardship can't pay struggling repayments lost job reduced hours illness hardship notice 21 days change contract
documents.text: A customer who can't meet repayments on a credit contract can tell the lender, verbally or in writing; this is a hardship notice. The lender must respond in writing within 21 days, or within that time ask for information it reasonably needs. Once the information is provided the lender has another 21 days to decide; if it isn't provided, the lender has 28 days from the request. The customer doesn't need to use the word hardship.

documents.title: Financial hardship: support options
documents.keywords: hardship help options pause repayments reduce extend term interest only deferral support assistance specialist
documents.text: Options a hardship specialist can consider include a short repayment pause, reduced repayments for a set period, extending the loan term, or switching to interest-only for a time. Each option has costs, for example more interest over the life of the loan, so a specialist assesses the customer's situation first; nothing is approved on the first call. While a hardship request is being assessed, the bank pauses collection activity on that account.

documents.title: Free financial counselling
documents.keywords: financial counsellor free help debt helpline support
documents.text: The National Debt Helpline on 1800 007 007 offers free, confidential financial counselling.

documents.title: Disputing a card transaction
documents.keywords: dispute transaction duplicate charged twice wrong amount not received refund chargeback merchant
documents.text: Customers can dispute a card transaction that was charged twice, charged at the wrong amount, or paid for goods or services that never arrived. It helps to contact the merchant first. The bank investigates and may raise a chargeback under card scheme rules; card schemes set time limits, so disputes should be raised as soon as possible. The outcome depends on the investigation, so no refund can be promised when a dispute is lodged. Investigations usually take up to 45 days.

documents.title: Unauthorised transactions
documents.keywords: unauthorised fraud didn't make payment someone used my card stolen card liability
documents.text: Under the ePayments Code, which subscribing banks follow, customers generally aren't liable for unauthorised transactions if they took reasonable care to protect their card and passcodes. The customer should report the transaction promptly. Each case depends on the investigation.

documents.title: Suspected fraud or scams: what to do now
documents.keywords: fraud scam security lock card stolen hacked code password phishing remote access what should i do
documents.text: If a card may be compromised, lock it straight away in the app and keep it locked until a replacement arrives. Never share passwords, PINs or one-time codes; the bank never asks for them. If someone has remote access to a device, disconnect it from the internet. Scams can be reported to Scamwatch, and identity theft support is available from IDCARE. Suspected fraud is handled by the fraud team as a priority.

documents.title: Making a complaint
documents.keywords: complaint unhappy dissatisfied escalate afca ombudsman how long response 30 days formal complaint
documents.text: Any expression of dissatisfaction where a response is expected counts as a complaint, even if the word complaint isn't used. Under ASIC Regulatory Guide 271 the bank must give a final response within 30 calendar days, or 21 days for complaints about hardship or default notices. If the customer isn't satisfied, or the deadline passes, they can go to AFCA for free on 1800 931 678 or at afca.org.au.

documents.title: Why identity is checked
documents.keywords: why identity verification privacy security check details secure
documents.text: Banks must take reasonable steps to protect personal information from unauthorised access and disclosure, so they confirm a caller's identity before discussing accounts. The check should match the sensitivity of the request.
